Starlink Mini USB-C Power Requirements

The Starlink Mini can run from a USB-C PD (Power Delivery) source, but it requires the correct voltage, sufficient wattage, and a compatible power cable.

Specification

	

Requirement




USB-C protocol

	

USB Power Delivery (USB-PD)




Recommended voltage

	

20V DC




Minimum USB-C PD output

	

100W (20V × 5A)




Typical operating consumption

	

25–40W




Recommended cable

	

USB-C to Starlink Mini DC power cable




USB-C cable rating

	

5A / 100W or higher

Important: Although the Starlink Mini typically consumes only 25–40W, a 30W or 45W USB-C charger may not work reliably. The USB-C power source needs enough capacity for startup and peak loads.

Compatible USB-C power sources

USB-C output

	

Compatibility




20V × 3A = 60W

	

 Not supported




20V × 3.25A = 65W

	

 Not supported




20V × 5A = 100W

	

 Supported




20V × 5A = 140W-rated charger

	

 Supported if 20V/5A is available

Starlink's official specification confirms a minimum 100W USB-PD source with 20V/5A output when using its USB-C cable. 
Starlink Help Center
+1

Make sure the power bank or charger supports 100W on a single USB-C port, not just 100W combined across multiple ports.

One distinction: the Mini itself accepts 12–48V DC, but that doesn't mean its USB-C adapter supports every voltage in that range.
